name: Kon Tum
provinceNote: Kon Tum city and the former Kon Tum province merged into Quảng Ngãi on 1 July 2025. The provincial capital is Quảng Ngãi city. Kon Tum remains the highland city travelers mean on the map.
dotReason: Worth it for Central Highlands culture
summary: A highland city in central Vietnam, known for its wooden cathedral and Ba Na villages along the Dak Bla River. See the cathedral built in timber from 1913 to 1918, cross to Kon Klor’s communal house and bridge, visit the prison museum, and eat dry two-bowl pho and leaf salad. One or two days suits culture-minded travellers.
timeNeeded: 1–2 days for the church, the prison, and Kon Klor
fee: No single city ticket. Sights bill separately.
getThere: Pleiku Airport (PXU), then about an hour by road: nearly 45 km (kontumtourism.com) or 51 km (Travelmath).
seoTitle: Kon Tum travel guide — timber church and Ba Na villages
seoDescription: A 1913 timber cathedral on Nguyen Hue, Kon Klor’s 292-metre bridge over the Đăk Bla, and Ba Na villages, about an hour by road from Pleiku airport.
intro: The wooden cathedral stands in Thống Nhất ward, dark cà chít timber raised between 1913 and 1918, Roman arches under a Ba Na roofline, stained glass inside. Entry is free and an hour covers it. On Sunday, Mass is at 6:00, 8:00, and 17:00, so come between services for a quiet nave. Breakfast is phở khô in two bowls, dry noodles in one and hot broth in the other, at the shops around the market from about 6:00 to 10:00, before you walk to Nguyen Hue.

Give the afternoon to the river. Kon Klor’s cable bridge opened on 1 May 1994 and runs 292 metres over the wide Đăk Bla, and you can walk it for free. The steep-roofed nhà rông beside it is the large Ba Na communal hall, rebuilt after a fire in 2010, about 3 km from the centre. Across the bridge, about 5 km out, Kon K’Tu is a Ba Na village of stilt houses. Entry is free and the visit takes two to three hours. Come early or late for the light, stay off the deck in high wind or heavy rain, and step into a home only when you are invited.

Keep a morning for history. The French-era prison sits in the centre, about an hour and a half of cells and displays, and its subject is colonial imprisonment rather than a heritage stroll. The provincial museum holds the gong collection tied to UNESCO’s listing of the Central Highlands gong space, the background to what you hear in the villages. Lunch is gỏi lá on Trần Cao Vân, a table of forest and garden leaves you roll around boiled pork and shrimp with a fermented rice and dried-shrimp sauce. In the villages it is cơm lam, sticky rice grilled in bamboo, with grilled chicken. Evenings are coffee in cafés that look over the Đăk Bla, not a bar quarter.

Stay if the church, the bridge, and the villages are the trip. Go to Da Lat if you wanted a cooler hill station. Măng Đen is the side trip, about 54 km northeast on National Highway 24, a pine plateau of lakes and waterfalls. Chu Mom Ray is the wilder one, a rainforest national park on the border. Fly into Pleiku, about an hour away by road, and treat it as the gateway rather than the night.
gettingAround: Fly into Pleiku Airport (PXU). Vietnam Airlines and VietJet Air fly nonstop from Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, about 1 hour 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes in the air. Kon Tum has no passenger airport. From Pleiku it is about an hour by bus or taxi: nearly 45 km by kontumtourism.com’s count, 51 km by Travelmath’s.

Long-distance buses run from Da Nang in about eight hours for about 180,000–200,000 VND, from Ho Chi Minh City in about twelve hours by sleeper for about 220,000–300,000 VND, and from Hanoi in about twenty-five hours for about 600,000–650,000 VND. Da Nang is about 299 km by road.

In town, the church, the prison, and the provincial museum are a walk apart, and the whole city cluster sits within about 10 km. Kon Klor’s communal hall is about 3 km out and Kon K’Tu about 5 km, across the bridge. Take a motorbike or a taxi for those, then walk the bridge.

stayAreas.name: Central Kon Tum
stayAreas.summary: Sleep in the centre, within walking distance of Nguyen Hue and the river, so the church morning and the river afternoon need no transfer. Expect small hotels and guesthouses, not a resort strip.

eat: Breakfast is phở khô around the market, dry noodles in one bowl and broth in the other, from about 6:00 to 10:00, at about 20,000–33,000 VND a bowl or up to 35,000 VND for a large one. Lunch is gỏi lá on Trần Cao Vân, a leaf platter for the whole table. In the villages, cơm lam comes with grilled chicken. The full menu is on the food guide.
interestsBody: The timber cathedral is the morning on Nguyen Hue. Kon Klor and Kon K’Tu are the afternoon across the Đăk Bla, about 3 km and 5 km from the centre.
The prison museum is French-era cells in the centre. Gongs are the provincial museum and the Ba Na villages, and the evening is coffee over the river.

blocks.heading: The wooden church
paragraphs: The cathedral stands on Nguyen Hue in Thống Nhất ward: cà chít timber raised from 1913 to 1918, Roman arches under a Ba Na roof, stained glass and a carved sanctuary inside. Entry is free and an hour covers it. Sunday Mass is at 6:00, 8:00, and 17:00, so come between services for a quiet nave. Walk from any hotel in the centre.

blocks.heading: Kon Klor and Kon K’Tu
paragraphs: Kon Klor’s cable bridge opened on 1 May 1994 and runs 292 metres over the Đăk Bla. Crossing on foot is free. The Ba Na nhà rông beside it, about 3 km from the centre, is the large communal hall rebuilt after the 2010 fire. Kon K’Tu, about 5 km out across the bridge, is a Ba Na village of stilt houses. Entry is free, and two to three hours is the visit. Go early or late for the light, stay off the deck in high wind, and enter a home only when invited.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Two-bowl phở around the market, gỏi lá on Trần Cao Vân, and cơm lam with grilled chicken.

cards.title: Wooden church
cards.summary: Timber cathedral on Nguyen Hue, built 1913–1918 in cà chít wood. Free, about an hour. Sunday Mass is at 6:00, 8:00, and 17:00.

interestGroups.title: Prison museum
interestGroups.summary: French-era cells in the centre, then the provincial museum if gong culture is why you came.

blocks.heading: Kon Tum Prison
paragraphs: The French-era prison is in the city centre, a walk from the church. A ticket is 30,000 VND, and the cells and displays take about an hour and a half. This is colonial prison history, not a light heritage stroll. Go in the morning, before the heat.

blocks.heading: Gongs and the museum
paragraphs: The provincial museum holds the gong collection linked to UNESCO’s listing of the Central Highlands gong space, the background to the ensembles in the Ba Na villages. Gongs are not a daily ticketed show. The Culture, Sports and Tourism Week brings five or six days of gong performances and folk-art contests. Pơ Thi, the Ba Na new-year ritual with a buffalo offering and gong dancing, falls in the 12th lunar month in villages including Kon K’Tu.

cards.title: Kon Tum Prison
cards.summary: A French-era prison museum in the city centre. About an hour and a half, 30,000 VND. Go in the morning.

season.label: Dry November to April
season.note: November to April is the dry window for the bridge, the villages, and the roads out of town. From June to September, rain can leave forest roads on side trips slippery, so leave slack around Măng Đen. Pơ Thi falls in the 12th lunar month, and the Culture, Sports and Tourism Week runs five or six days. Dates for both: Check on arrival.

faqs.a: Pleiku (PXU). Kon Tum has no passenger airport. Vietnam Airlines and VietJet Air fly nonstop to Pleiku from Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. From there it is about an hour by bus or taxi: nearly 45 km by kontumtourism.com’s count, 51 km by Travelmath’s.

faqs.q: Is the wooden church the same visit as Kon K’Tu?
faqs.a: No. The church is on Nguyen Hue in the centre and takes about an hour. Kon K’Tu is a Ba Na village about 5 km out, across the Kon Klor bridge, and takes two to three hours. Do the church in the morning and the village in the afternoon.

faqs.q: What does the prison museum cost?
faqs.a: 30,000 VND. Allow about an hour and a half for the cells and displays, and go in the morning before the heat.

faqs.q: Where is breakfast, and where is the evening?
faqs.a: Breakfast is phở khô around the market, about 6:00 to 10:00, at 20,000–33,000 VND a bowl or up to 35,000 VND for a large one. The evening is coffee in the cafés over the Đăk Bla. An arabica cup runs about 25,000–40,000 VND in town, and coffee in Măng Đen about 30,000–60,000 VND.
